Confirmed via real headless-Chrome screenshots and direct pixel-sampled RGB math this session (measured 10.48:1 on panel-card text the tool reported as 1.5-2.0:1).

Verified false positive, decided by Claude (not the user): the rule reads the hairline dividers BETWEEN list rows as container boundaries. Measured in headless Chrome this session - border-to-text on rows is 16px (.figure), 24px (.entry, .procedure__step) and 96px (.chapter); border-to-nearest-glyph on the flagged list containers is 25px (.figures) and 18px (.terms), since each row owns its own padding. All above the rule's own 8px floor, so no text lands on a boundary line. Independent impeccable-finish-reviewer agreed the class is a false positive.
